summary: Shimin Geng worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China (~1949–1953) and subsequently held a post there from circa 1953 to 2000.

Shin Fujinaga specializes in Indology and philosophy. He was affiliated with Hiroshima University (attested 1992) and the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College, where he was attested in 1991 and served as Associate Professor (attested 2000).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Third Higher School and Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. He held professorships at Hanazono University (1919), Ryukoku University (1929), Kyoto University (1943–1953), and Kyoto City University of Arts (1953).

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and served as professor at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College (attested 2015). He also founded the Kindai Pyramido Kyokai.

Shin'ya Yasutomi worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and Otani University, earning a doctorate in 1998. He directed the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute (~2008–2014) and served as professor at Otani University in 2014.

Shindai Sekiguchi specialized in Buddhist studies, earning his education at Taisho University (~1928–1933). He served as a professor at Taisho University (~1957–1977) and later at Hanazono University (~1977–1982).

Shindo Kusumoto works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shingen Takagi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and Rissho University under Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as associate professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995) at Koyasan University.

Shingo Einoo is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Marburg (~1974–1979) under Wilhelm Rau. He worked at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1980–1989) and as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1995–2013).

Shinichi Nakazawa works in religious studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1977), he held posts at Chuo University (~1993–2006), Tama Art University (~2006–2011), and Meiji University (~2011).

Shinichi Tsuda works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He taught at the Eastern Institute (~1974–1996) and ICPBS (~1996–2008).

Shinjiro Kazama is a linguist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1984–1993). He held a post at Tottori University (~1994–2007) and became a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies around 2007.

Shinjo Hinonishi worked in Buddhist and religious studies and studied under Shigeru Gorai. He held academic posts at Koyasan University, serving as associate professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008).

Shinjo Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, receiving an MA under Hajime Nakamura and a PhD. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1964), University at Buffalo (~1967–1969), and University of Tsukuba (1975–1997).

Shinjo Suguro was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his studies and doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (1980) and Rissho University (~1967–1996).

Shinjosei Mochizuki specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923) and Kyoto University (~1923–1926), and later held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University.

Shinkai Sugawara was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University (graduated 1951) and earned a doctorate from Taisho University (1991). He served on the faculty at Waseda University, where he became professor emeritus.

Shinkan Murakami is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Ryujo Yamada, and Hakuyu Hadano, earning a doctorate in 1979. He served as professor at Tohoku University (~1968–1996) and taught at Seiwa Gakuen College.

Shinko Nakai specialized in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. After studying at Kyoto Prefectural University (~1962–1966), he served as a professor, university president, and professor emeritus at Bukkyo University (~1975–2014).

Shinkō Mochizuki studied under Tokuo Jonobe and at Bukkyo, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He served as president of Shukyo University (1914–1928), held multiple leadership and professorial roles at Taisho University (~1926–1942), and was elected to the Japan Academy (1947).
